key_concepts: Compounds are made of elements chemically bonded by electrostatic forces.
Ionic compounds form when a metal transfers valence electrons to a nonmetal.
Covalent compounds form when nonmetals share valence electrons.
Chemical formulas and names indicate the types of elements and number of atoms in a compou
Ionic compounds typically have crystal lattice structures and high melting points.
Covalent compounds typically have low melting points and may be soft or flexible.
Solid ionic compounds do not conduct electricity because their ions are not free to move.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity when dissolved in water because their ions become free
Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity in solid or aqueous solution.
